steps.title: Record the email that needs a reply, with its source
do: Find the email in Paul's Sent Items with the Microsoft 365 connector (outlook_email_search, `recipient` filter, no folder). If it is a draft Paul has not sent yet, there is nothing to find: use today's date as the date sent. Record EVERY try, failures too:
python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --route m365|zapier|device --result found|failed --note "what you did and what came back"

Then record the email: python3 {scripts}/run.py email {run} --senders "a@x.com,b@y.com" --subject "the subject" --sent DD/MM/YYYY --why "why a reply is needed" --source "where these came from" [--folder "client folder to also watch for a dropped file"]

The program refuses a missing or bad address, Paul's own address, a date in the future, an email so old that the watching time is over, and a missing reason or source. If you cannot say why a reply is needed, the email does not need tracking: tell Paul and stop.
steps.proof: the email is recorded with its sources, the lookup try is logged, and the program accepted every fact

steps.title: The program builds the two scheduled-task files
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}
It writes out/watch.json (the hourly watcher), out/flag.json (the one-time silence flag) and out/plan.txt. You never type or edit any of them.
steps.proof: the plan follows every rule and is exactly what the program builds from the email

steps.title: Show Paul the plan (no question: it is his standing rule)
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py show {run}
Put the plan it prints in your reply. There is no question to ask: Paul made this a standing rule and nothing is sent to anyone. If you rebuild, show it again.
steps.proof: the plan was shown for exactly this build

steps.title: Create the two scheduled tasks with exactly the program's settings
do: Follow the rules below, then record what each create_trigger call returned (copy the values; do not retype them from the files):
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} watch.id <the id>        python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} watch.connector_ok yes|no
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} flag.id <the id>         python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} flag.connector_ok yes|no
connector_ok is `no` if the result warns that the task stores no connectors: then STOP and tell Paul.
steps.proof: both tasks were created and the tool returned an id for each without a connector warning

steps.title: Read the tasks back and let the program compare them with the plan
do: Follow the rules below. Call list_triggers and record, for each of the two tasks, what it shows:
watch.name  watch.cron  watch.enabled yes|no  watch.next_run  watch.new_session yes|no
flag.name  flag.run_once_at  flag.enabled yes|no  flag.next_run  flag.new_session yes|no
with: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} KEY VALUE
Save each task's stored instruction text exactly as list_triggers shows it to a file, then: python3 {scripts}/run.py promptfile {run} watch --file <file>    and the same for flag.
steps.proof: what list_triggers shows equals the plan: names, schedule, fire time, switched on, fresh chat, instruction text

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final
Put the short audit it prints in your reply exactly as it is: one line per check with a green tick or a red cross, one closing line for what is only attested. Nothing longer.
Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
